title: Prins-Regent-pudding (Prince Regent Pudding)
description: A pudding made with bread, sweet almonds, and rusks.
steps: Cream the butter and sugar until the mixture becomes white and fluffy.
Add the yolks, the grated bread, the chopped almonds and spices to taste.
Last, carefully fold in the beaten egg whites.
Pour the batter into a buttered and bread-crumbed mold and bake in a water bath on the stove for 2 hours.
Serve the pudding warm with foam sauce.

title: Prinsesskakor (Princess Cakes)
description: A cake made with egg whites, wheat flour, and bitter almonds.
steps: Wash the butter and sift the flour on the work table.
Distribute the butter in flakes and place on top of the flour along with sugar, the blanched and finely grated almonds, and egg whites (not beaten to peaks).
Work all ingredients together into a smooth, cohesive dough.
Roll out quite thick and cut out small cakes with a measure.
Brush with egg white and sprinkle with almonds and sugar.
Bake until light brown in moderate oven heat.

title: Prästgårdslimpor (Parsonage Loaves)
description: Prepared with rye flour, ale, and wheat flour.
steps: Pour the rye flour into a bowl and stir it with the drink, which should be heated to about 80°, stir the mass well, cover with a baking cloth and let it stand in a warm place overnight.

Early the next morning add 1 kg of the wheat flour, the lukewarm milk and the yeast mixed with salt, and work the dough with the hand until it becomes even and smooth, and add more flour so that the dough becomes quite firm, after which it is covered and allowed to rise to double its size.

The fat, syrup and spices are mixed in a saucepan, brought to a boil, allowed to cool and worked into the risen dough together with wheat flour, after which the dough is placed in a warm place and allowed to rise again.
It is then treated, shaped and baked as in the previous recipe.

title: Pudding av kalvstek (Veal Pudding)
description: A pudding made with veal, veal or chicken or meat, and bread.

ingredients.name: 4 hg. roasted, boneless veal or chicken meat
ingredients.sourceText: 4 hg. roasted, boneless veal or chicken meat

ingredients.name: butter (10 g) for the onion
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tbsp. butter (10 g) for the onion

ingredients.name: butter (10 g) for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tbsp. butter (10 g) for the mold

ingredients.name: crushed rusks for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tbsp. crushed rusks for the mold

steps: Finely chop the roasted meat.
Grind the raw meat 3 times through a meat grinder and mix with the roasted meat.
Lightly brown the panade in 1 tbsp. of butter, place in a bowl and immediately mix in the cold butter.
Stir in the egg yolks one at a time, along with spices and the finely chopped onion fried in butter.
Mix the meat well with the panade and add enough cream so the forcemeat becomes like thin porridge.
Fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Pour the mixture into a buttered and breadcrumb-lined mold.
Bake in a water bath in the oven for approximately 1 hour.
Serve with leftover roasting sauce, mushroom sauce, or simply with clarified butter.

title: Pudding av kött och risgryn (Meat and Rice Pudding)
description: A pudding made with meat, rice, and onions.

ingredients.name: boneless fried or cooked meat
ingredients.sourceText: 500 g boneless fried or cooked meat

ingredients.name: butter for the mold (10 g)
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tablespoon butter for the mold (10 g)

steps: Cut the meat into thin slices or chop finely (do not grind). Peel, chop and brown the onion in the butter in a frying pan, add the meat and brown it well, season it and mix with the hot gravy or broth.

Rinse the rice grains with cold water, scald in hot water, add to the boiling milk and let cook until soft, then drain, immediately mix with the cold butter and let cool. Add the beaten egg yolks with the salt and finally fold in the stiffly beaten egg whites.

Butter a pie mold and sprinkle with crushed rusks. Layer the meat and rice alternately in the mold, the top layer should be rice, sprinkled with crushed rusks. Bake the pudding in the oven for about 30-40 minutes. Serve with gravy or clarified butter.
Instead of onion, finely chopped salt or pickled cucumber can be used. The pudding can be made simpler by using cream instead of butter and omitting the eggs in the rice.

title: Pudding av sidfläsk och kål (Pork Belly and Cabbage Pudding)
description: A pudding made with cabbage, salted pork belly, and water.
steps: Rinse the pork, place it in cold water and let it cook for 1/2 hour.
Remove the outer leaves of the cabbage head, loosen the remaining leaves from the core and cut them into coarse strips.
Bring water to a boil with a little salt, place the cabbage in it and let it cook 5 minutes without a lid, after which place it on a sieve so that the water drains well.
Cut the pork into slices and taste the broth.
In a pudding mold with a lid, layer the cabbage and pork alternately, and add 1/2 liter of the broth.
Put the lid on and let the pudding cook in a water bath on the stove for approximately 2 hours.
Serve with brown cream sauce.

title: Päron i Vaniljkräm (Pears in Vanilla Cream)
description: Prepared with pears, cream, and vanilla pod.
steps: Boil the cream with vanilla and sugar until it has acquired sufficient vanilla flavor.
Thicken with potato flour mixed in a little cream, let boil briefly and remove from heat.
Whisk the egg yolks together in a bowl and add the cream with vigorous whisking.
Return the cream to heat and let it simmer but not boil.
When thickened, pour onto a round platter.
Peel and halve the pears.
Make a clear syrup from the sugar and water; add the pears and cook until soft, then arrange in a ring on the cream.
Soak the apricots in warm water for a few hours before cooking, then cook in the same water.
When soft, strain them and season the sauce with sugar and pour over the pears.
Place a halved berry on each pear.
Put the platter in a moderate oven for about 10 minutes, then serve.

description: Prepared with pears, cream, and vanilla bean.
steps: Heat the cream with the vanilla bean and sugar until it has sufficient vanilla flavor. title: Päron ä la Melba (Pears à la Melba)
description: Prepared with pears, white wine, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: 6 French or other good, loose pears
ingredients.sourceText: 6 French or other good, loose pears

ingredients.name: spun sugar or 50 grams roasted sweet almond
ingredients.sourceText: spun sugar or 50 grams roasted sweet almond

steps: Make a clear syrup from the sugar, water, and wine, and let it cool.
Peel the pears, carefully remove the bloom at the end, scrape the stem, and place the pears directly in the sugar syrup and cook until soft, but they must not mash in the least.
Remove them with a slotted spoon and let them cool.
Pack the vanilla glace (see Vanilla Glace) in the bottom of a beautiful compote dish or silver bowl.

Place the pears on the glace, pour cold red apricot sauce over them and garnish on top with plenty of spun sugar (see spun sugar) or with almond that has been blanched, cut into strips and roasted in the oven together with 1 tablespoon sugar.
Prepare the apricot sauce as in recipe 462, but colour it with carmine so that it becomes beautifully red, before thickening it with potato flour.
Instead of apricot sauce, a sauce made from strawberry juice can be used.

title: Päronkaka (Pear Cake)
description: A cake made with pears, wheat flour, and lemon.

ingredients.name: ½ tsk. butter for the form
ingredients.sourceText: ½ tsk. butter for the form

steps: Peel the pears, cut them in half, and remove the cores.
From the sugar and water boil a clear syrup, and in this cook the pears until they are soft.
Place them on the bottom of a buttered pie form.
Bring the milk to a boil, stir in the sifted flour quickly, let the mixture cook 10 minutes and then cool.
Meanwhile mix in the cold butter, sugar, lemon peel and egg yolks one at a time.
Last, fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Pour the mixture over the pears and place the cake in moderate oven heat to bake for a time.
Test with a whisk and serve after most of the heat has subsided.

title: Päronkaka (Pear Cake)
description: A cake made with white wine, pears, and sugar.

ingredients.name: butter (10 gr) for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tbsp butter (10 gr) for the pan

steps: From the sugar, wine and water, a clear syrup is boiled.
The pears are rinsed, dried, peeled, split lengthwise, freed from the cores, placed in the sugar syrup and left to cook until soft.
They are taken out and placed in a greased pie pan.
The syrup is boiled down until it is thick, and poured over the pears.
Butter and flour are fried for 2 minutes, the milk is added and the mixture is left to boil for 5 minutes.
The lemon zest and sugar are added, and the mixture is left to cool, after which the egg yolks are stirred in one at a time, and finally the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks are folded in.
The cream is poured immediately over the fruit, and the pudding is baked in a water bath in the oven for approximately 1 hour, or until the mass is baked through when tested with a whisk.
Served slightly cooled with or without whipped cream.
Instead of pears, compote of apples or plums can be used.

title: Pösmunkar à la Skogshöjd (Puff Pastry Puffs à la Skogshöjd)
description: A pastry dish made with cream, bitter almonds, and sweet almonds.
steps: Butter a pot with a round bottom with 1/2 msk of the butter, pour in the cream, and add the sugar and the blanched and grated almond.
Let the cream boil up, add the rest of the butter, and whisk in the flour with a steel whisk.
Let the batter then cook until it releases from the pan.
Remove the pot from heat, work in the eggs one at a time, and stir the mixture for 10 minutes.
Form the mixture with two tablespoons into round balls the size of a small crust, which are cooked a beautiful golden brown in shortening.
The puffs should be formed as smooth as possible, and no more than 3 are cooked at a time.
The shortening should not be too hot, as the puffs will not then be able to swell.
Turn them with a slotted spoon, and when the puffs have a golden brown color on both sides, remove them with a slotted spoon and place them on absorbent paper on a warm sheet in the oven.
Sprinkle with sugar and serve warm with jam as a dessert, or with coffee or tea.

title: Queneller (Fish Quenelles)
description: Prepared with fish, cream, and white pepper.
steps: Remove the fish (do not scale), rinse and dry well, fillet and scrape finely (no scale or bone should go with it).
Pound it together with the butter in a stone mortar until the mass is fine and coherent, then mix with half of the cream and pass through a sieve.
In a bowl, mix the rest of the cream, egg yolks, salt, sugar, white pepper, and flour.
Add this mixture spoonful by spoonful to the fish mixture.
Work it for about 1.5 hours, then fold in the beaten egg whites.
Press the mixture through a pastry bag or paper cone into small oblong cakes on a buttered baking sheet.
Pour boiling water carefully over them, and let the quenelles cook slowly for 5-6 minutes.

title: Queneller av fiskfärs (Fish Quenelles)
description: Prepared with pike, white pepper, and cream.

ingredients.name: 4 hg. pike = 150 gr. scraped fish meat
ingredients.sourceText: 4 hg. pike = 150 gr. scraped fish meat

steps: Clean the pike (do not scale), rinse well and dry with a fish towel. Fillet it, loosen the backbone and scrape the fish meat finely; no scales or bones must be included.
Mix with the seasonings, pass 3 times through a meat grinder and pound with a wooden pestle in a stone mortar until a fine mass.
Whisk the egg and add it little by little along with the flour, while stirring the forcemeat vigorously.

Pass through a hair sieve, place in a small saucepan set in a bowl of ice (otherwise it will break when the cream is worked in) and add the cream by teaspoonful while stirring evenly, then taste the forcemeat carefully.

Brush a long pan with butter and let it cool. Place the forcemeat in a piping bag with smooth or fluted tip and pipe directly into the pan in the form of small balls or oblong shapes, placed very close together.

When all the quenelles are formed, place the pan to the side of the stove and add boiling salted water carefully until it stands level over them. Let the water come to a boil while shaking the pan slowly, then let it cook until the quenelles have swelled and feel firm, about 2-3 minutes.
Remove immediately with a slotted spoon and place in a soup bowl. Pour the hot consommé or broth over just before serving.

title: Rabarberkompott (Rhubarb Compote)
description: Prepared with rhubarb, sugar, and water.
steps: Cook the sugar and water together to make a clear, syrupy liquid
Rinse and dry the rhubarb stalks, peel thinly, and cut into 3 centimeter pieces
Place the thickest pieces first in the sugar liquid and cook until tender but not falling apart
Remove pieces with a silver fork as they become soft and place in a compote bowl
The smaller pieces require barely any cooking before becoming tender
Cook the syrup until it is clear and syrupy, then pour over the rhubarb
Serve cold with whipped cream

title: Rabarberkräm (Rhubarb Cream)
description: Prepared with rhubarb, flour or potato flour, and water.

ingredients.name: mondamin flour (23 grams) or 1/2 tablespoon potato flour (23 grams)
ingredients.sourceText: 1 1/2 tablespoons mondamin flour (23 grams) or 1/2 tablespoon potato flour (23 grams)

steps: Rinse and dry the rhubarb, peel very thinly and cut into 2 centimetre long pieces.
Make a clear syrup from the sugar and water, add the rhubarb and let it cook until soft but not falling apart.
Mix the flour with 2 tablespoons cold water and add it, then let the cream cook 5 minutes if thickened with mondamin, but 2 minutes if thickened with potato flour.
Pour it into a compote dish rinsed with lukewarm water and sprinkle with powdered sugar to prevent a skin from forming.
Serve with cream or milk.

title: Rabarberpaj (Rhubarb Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with rhubarb, sweet almonds, and bitter almonds.

ingredients.name: butter (10 gr) for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tbsp butter (10 gr) for the pan

ingredients.name: crushed rusks for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tbsp crushed rusks for the pan

steps: The butter is washed and worked together with the sugar, flour, the blanched and ground almonds and egg into a smooth dough, which is left to rest in a cold place for approximately 2 hours.
The rhubarb is peeled thinly and cut into 3 cm long pieces.

Two-thirds of the dough is rolled out and with it a greased baking sheet or frying pan is lined, after which the rhubarb is added in alternating layers with the sugar, and the dough edge is folded over.
The rest of the dough is rolled out to a lid, with which the pie is covered, and the edges are pressed down well.
The pie is baked in ordinary oven heat for approximately 1 hour, or until the rhubarb is soft and the dough is baked through when tested with a whisk.
It is taken out and left to stand for a quarter hour, after which it is turned out and served warm or cold with whipped cream or vanilla sauce.

title: Rabarbersaft (Rhubarb Juice)
description: Prepared with rhubarb, currants, and water.
steps: Rinse and dry the rhubarb and cut it into pieces. Rinse and strip the currants.
Place these together with the rhubarb in the water and let them cook with stirring until they are completely soft.
Pour the mass into cheesecloth to drain. Place the clear juice on the fire again together with the sugar and let it cook with constant skimming until it is completely clear and somewhat glossy.
Bottle the juice; cork the bottles and seal with resin.

title: Rabarbersufflé (Rhubarb Soufflé)
description: Prepared with rhubarb, sour cream, and sugar.
steps: Peel the rhubarb, cut it into pieces and cook it quickly until soft in the water together with the crushed sugar.
Stir the egg yolks with the cream, caster sugar and lemon zest until the mixture is foamy.
Beat the whites until stiff peaks form and fold them in gently.
Pour half of the mixture into a buttered, heat-resistant mold.
Drain the cooked and cooled rhubarb through a colander and place it in the mold.
Pour the remaining batter over it.
Bake the soufflé in moderate oven heat for about 1 hour.
Serve immediately with whipped cream.

title: Rabarbertårta (Rhubarb Tart)
description: A pastry dish made with rhubarb, almond, and wheat flour.
steps: Make a regular shortcrust pastry from the butter, flour, blanched and grated almond, and sugar, and let it set.
Peel the rhubarb, cut it into pieces and cook together with the sugar until soft.
Remove with a slotted spoon and let it drain.
Line the bottom of a ring form and 30 cm. of the edge with the pastry, and bake it.
Spread the rhubarb on the tart.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and then carefully mix with vanilla and granulated sugar.
Garnish the tart with the meringue mixture and put it in the oven again to get a nice light yellow color.
Serve with whipped cream or vanilla sauce.

title: Ragout på gås (Goose Ragout)
description: Prepared with goose, mushrooms, and sauce.

ingredients.name: Rester av gås (goose leftovers) 3-4 hg. kött (meat)
ingredients.sourceText: Rester av gås (goose leftovers) 3-4 hg. kött (meat)

steps: Cut the meat into nice pieces.
Chop the carcass, place in cold water with salt, and let cook approximately 1 1/2 hours to make a good broth.
Blanch the mushrooms for 1/2 hour, let drain, wrap in cloth and cut into fine cubes.
Sauté the mushrooms in butter until clear, then press them out with a spoon and fry the flour with the butter for 2 minutes.
Add the sauce and enough broth to make a thickened gravy, let cook 5 minutes.
Add the meat along with the mushrooms and the blanched, pitted prunes.
The dish should then only simmer, not boil.
Peel the apples, cut into four wedges and cook in a mixture of sugar and water until soft but not falling apart.
Arrange the ragout on a warm serving dish, garnish with apple wedges and small browned potatoes and serve as a breakfast dish.

title: Ragu på vilt (Game Ragout)
description: Prepared with meat or game, bouillon or water, and bouillon.

ingredients.name: 3—4 hg. cooked, boneless meat of poultry or game
ingredients.sourceText: 3—4 hg. cooked, boneless meat of poultry or game

steps: Ragu on game is usually used as filling in vol-au-vents, puff pastry cases, pastries, risoles and for croquettes etc.

The meat is separated from the bones and cut into small cubes or oblong pieces, the bones are crushed and cooked in the bouillon (or water, with 4 gr. solid meat extract and salt) with the cloves, until the bouillon has a good game flavor, then it is strained.
Butter and flour are fried for 2 minutes; the bouillon is thinned in and the sauce is allowed to boil for 5 minutes.
The meat is added and warmed in the sauce but must not boil, as it will then become tough.
The preparation is seasoned with currant jelly and red wine and spices, if needed.

title: Ragù på vilt (Game Ragout)
description: Prepared with meat or game, bouillon or water, and jelly.

ingredients.sourceText: 3—4 hg. cooked, boneless meat of poultry or game

steps: Ragout of game is usually used as filling in vol-au-vents, pastries, risoles and for croquettes, etc.

The meat is loosened from the bones and cut into small cubes or oblong pieces, the bones are crushed and cooked in the bouillon (or water, with 4 gr. meat extract added and salt) with the cloves, until the bouillon obtains a good game flavor, when it is strained.
Butter and flour are fried for 2 minutes; the bouillon is thinned and the sauce is allowed to boil for 5 minutes.
The meat is added and heated in the sauce but must not boil, as it then becomes tough.
The dish is seasoned with lingonberry jelly and red wine and spices, if needed.

title: Randig blanc-mangé (Striped Blanc-mangé)
description: Prepared with almond, cream, and gelatin.
steps: Blanch the almonds and grate them.
Make a syrup from the sugar and water, in which the almond is allowed to boil 10 minutes.
To further draw out the almond flavor, let the syrup stand beside the fire for another 20 minutes, then strain it.
Whisk the cream to stiff peaks, add the sugar syrup, and finally the gelatin dissolved in a little lukewarm water.
Divide the mixture into three equal parts.
Flavor one part with the zest and juice of the oranges; color the second part with carmine and the third with spinach green.
Rinse a pretty mold with cold water and sprinkle with sugar.
Place the green mixture on the bottom and set it out to stiffen.
On top of this place the white mixture, and when it has set, the red mixture.
When the blanc-mangé is to be served, dip the mold in lukewarm water and turn out the pudding.

steps: Prepare the forcemeats as in recipe no. 67, and stir in the truffles cut into fine strips.
Layer the forcemeats alternately in an elongated, buttered bread mold that holds approximately 1 1/2 liters.
Bind the mold over with buttered paper and bake the forcemeat in a water bath in the oven for approximately 1 hour.
Test with a whisk and turn out onto an elongated platter to cool.
Prepare the aspic as in recipe no. 181.
Slice the forcemeat into approximately 7 mm thick slices and arrange them on large platters with small spaces between.

title: Rapphönssoufflé (Partridge Soufflé)
description: Prepared with partridges, cream, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: butter (20 gr) for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 1 tbsp butter (20 gr) for the mold

steps: Pluck the partridges, remove the innards, rinse well and skin them.
Cut all meat from the carcasses and scrape thoroughly free of sinews and membranes.
Pass the meat 3 times through the meat grinder, mix with the butter and grind 3 more times.
Place the mixture in a bowl and add half the cream bit by bit while stirring vigorously.
Pass the mixture through a fine sieve and stir in the egg yolks one at a time, along with the flour and seasonings, and if desired, finely cut truffle.
Stir the mixture for 1/2 hour, during which time the remaining cream, whipped until stiff, is added bit by bit.
Finally, carefully fold in the egg whites beaten until stiff peaks form.
Taste and adjust seasonings.
Pour into a well-buttered and breadcrumb-lined ring mold and cook in a water bath in the oven for about 1 1/4 hours.
Turn out, garnish with fine vegetables or stuffed tomatoes and serve immediately as a middle course with gravy made from the poultry bones.
The same method can be used for soufflé of other game or domestic poultry.

title: Renstek (Roast Reindeer)
description: Prepared with skimmed milk or milk, lard, and broth.

ingredients.name: skimmed milk or drinking milk
ingredients.sourceText: 3 litres skimmed milk or drinking milk

steps: If the meat is frozen, it should lie in milk or drinking milk until just thawed.
If unfrozen, wash it very thoroughly with a cloth dipped in hot water and beat with a damp meat mallet.
Dry the meat well and remove all membranes, then lard it and rub with the remaining salt and tie it so it takes a beautiful shape.

Brown the butter in a roasting pan, place the meat in and brown it well on all sides, then add liquid, first with the boiling broth, then with the boiling cream or milk, and let it roast with a tightly closed lid until tender, about 3½ hours, turning it a few times and basting every 10 minutes.
Slice the meat into thin slices, place on a warm platter and pour over a couple of tablespoons of sauce.
Garnish with browned potatoes, salad or parsley and serve with reduced sauce (see no. 429), mixed with thick cream, as well as green salad and sour salads or lingonberry jelly.

title: Renstek (Roasted Reindeer)
description: Prepared with skim milk or liquid, lard, and broth.

ingredients.name: skim milk or drinking liquid

title: Revstek (Rib Roast)
description: Prepared with smoked ham, carrots, and shallots.
steps: Chop the meat before weighing it.
Cut away the rib bones, but leave the backbone.
Clean away most of the fat on the outside, rub the meat with salt and lard or cover with ham slices, which are fastened with kitchen twine dipped in boiling water.
Oil a long pan with cold butter to the size the meat occupies, place in the prepared and thickly sliced carrots and the peeled and quartered onions, and place the meat on top with the outside up.
Place in a warm oven and baste often with the butter until nicely browned (the vegetables should not burn), then dilute gradually with the bouillon and wine.
Baste the meat every 10 minutes and let it roast until tender, which is tested with a whisk; remove and cut off the strings.
Slice the roast, place on a warm platter, garnish with vegetable patties or potato croquettes and kale or parsley.
Serve with brown sauce.

title: Risgryn- och Apelsipudding (Rice and Orange Pudding)
description: A pudding made with rice, oranges, and cream.
steps: Rinse the rice grains, scald them in hot water, add to boiling water and let them cook until soft, about 20 minutes.
Drain the rice in a sieve and rinse with cold water, letting it drain well.
Peel the oranges, carefully remove the white pith, cut them into small cubes, remove the seeds and mix with sugar.
Whip the cream into stiff peaks.
Rinse the gelatin with cold water, cut it into pieces and dissolve in three tbsp. hot water.
Mix the rice grains with the orange cubes and cream, and lastly add the gelatin.
Pour the mixture into a water-rinsed and sugar-dusted mold and let it stand on ice for about 3 hours, or until set.
Loosen the pudding around the edges with a pointed knife, turn it out onto a flat glass dish with pastry paper, garnish with orange segments and serve with orange sauce.

Peel the apples, cut them into fine sections and add along with the sugar when the porridge has cooked about 15 minutes.
Let the porridge then cook slowly until the groats and apples are completely soft, or about 1 1/2 hours, stirring often so that it does not burn.
Season the porridge with more sugar if needed, and add the punch if desired.
Serve with cream or milk.

Coarse groats can also be used for this porridge.

steps: Prepare the puff pastry as in no. 33, place in a napkin and let rest a few hours.
Prepare the stew as in no. 47. When it has simmered with the egg yolk, immediately add the gelatin, rinsed in cold water and dissolved in 1 tbsp. hot water.

description: Prepared with onion, rice, and broth.
steps: Peel the onion, chop it finely and fry it well in 1 hg. of the butter in a saucepan.
Add the rinsed rice grains together with the finely ground saffron and stir over gentle heat until well blended with the butter.
Add the broth, a little at a time, while stirring the grains frequently with a wooden spoon.
Allow the rice grains to cook slowly with a lid, stirring often, until the grains are soft and begin to break apart.
Season the dish with the remaining butter, Parmesan cheese, and the ham cut into fine cubes, and salt.
Serve as a breakfast or intermediate course.

title: Roast in Aspic (Stek i Gelé)
description: Prepared with beef or veal, carrot, and green beans.

ingredients.name: 6 hectograms leftover beef or veal roast
ingredients.sourceText: 6 hectograms leftover beef or veal roast

steps: The roast, which should be juicy and good, is cut into beautiful, even slices, which are laid on a large platter at even intervals.
The carrot is cut into slices and these are cut out into flowers with a vegetable cutter.
The beans are cut out into stalks and leaves.
With these flowers and leaves, garnish the meat slices.
Prepare the gelatin as in no. 181, and when it is cold, add the wine.
A little of the clear gelatin is poured onto the platter but should only just reach the garnish, otherwise it will flow around it.
When the first gelatin has set, pour on the remainder, which should cover the meat slices.
Place the platter in a cold place and after 2-3 hours, cut out the slices so that a border of gelatin extends beyond the slice.
Arrange a round platter with salad leaves and tomato wedges and lay the slices in a ring on the platter so that the flowers show.
Serve as a course with vegetable or potato salad.

title: Rosthammel (Roast Mutton)
description: Prepared with white pepper, carrot, and shallot.
steps: The meat, which should have hung so that it is tender, is beaten with a damp club, dried with a cloth, wrung in hot water, rubbed with a mixture of salt and pepper and brushed with parsley butter, which is made of 2 tbsp of the butter as in the previous recipe.

In a small long roasting pan or roasting pan, the rest of the butter, the scraped and sliced carrot and the peeled and cut shallot are placed. The roast is placed in and roasted in a warm oven for about 1 hour, during which it is basted frequently with the butter in the pan so that it does not dry out or burn.
A quarter of an hour before it is done, the boiling gravy is added.
Placed on a warm platter and carved at table. Served with vegetable or potato pasties and the gravy, which is strained and skimmed.

description: Prepared with mutton, onions, and butter.
steps: Wash the mutton saddle with a cloth dipped in hot water and beat very well.
Brown 2 tbsp of the butter in a long pan, place the saddle in it and put in the oven.
When it has a nice brown color, salt it and continue roasting until tender.
Parboil the onion, peel and cut into large wedges, which are browned in the remaining butter and served with the roast.
Strain the sauce, skim, and serve as gravy.

description: Prepared with turnips, potatoes, and butter or cream.
steps: Peel the turnips and cut them into small pieces and put them on to cook in salted water for about 30 minutes.
Peel the potatoes, cut them into slices and add them to cook with the turnips until everything is soft.
Drain the water, mash the potatoes and turnips with a fork.
Stir in the cold butter together with the milk.
Work the mash well and season with the spices.

title: Rotmos (Root Vegetable Mash)
description: Prepared with beef broth or pork or stock, potatoes, and cream.

ingredients.name: beef broth or pork stock

steps: The rutabaga is peeled (see page 338), cut into cubes, which are placed in the cold broth, and are allowed to boil until half soft or about 15 minutes.
The potato is peeled, cut into cubes and placed on top of the rutabaga, whereupon the root vegetables are allowed to boil until they are soft.
The excess stock is then drained off, and the roots are mashed with a fork.
The cold butter is added at once together with the boiled cream, while the mash is worked well with a fork.
It is seasoned carefully with spices and is served with salted meat, pork or sausage.

title: Rulad av ål (Rolled Eel)
description: Prepared with eel, vinegar, and fish stock.
steps: Skin the eel and cut it open along the back.
Remove the backbone and innards, rinse and dry the eel well and rub it with salt.
Roll it up fairly tightly from the head and tie it with string.
Place the roll in hot water together with the dill stalks, allspice berries and vinegar and let it simmer slowly until done, then remove it and let it cool.
Add gelatin to the stock and clarify with egg whites and strain through a cloth or cheesecloth.
Pour part of the clarified aspic onto a flat dish to set.
Slice the roll, place these slices on the set aspic, and pour the remaining aspic over, then set it again.
Separate the slices with a knife from each other so that a little aspic remains around each slice.
Arrange them in a ring on a platter and garnish with dill.

title: Rulader av rökt svinkarré (Rolls of Smoked Pork Loin)
description: A bread preparation made with pork, sardines, and bread.
steps: The pork loin should be lightly salted and only hot-smoked for approximately 2 hours.
Cut it into 12 slices, which are trimmed even at the edges.
On each slice place a sardine filet, roll the slices together and lay the rolls tightly next to each other in a frying pan.
On the bread slices, which should be 2 cm. thick, cut away the edges so that they have the same form as the rolls.
Fry them beautifully golden-brown in the butter and place on a warm serving platter.
Put the rolls into a hot oven and take them out when they are lightly browned.
Place them on the croutons (bread slices) and serve immediately to the smorgasbord.

title: Rullbakelser (Rolled Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with powdered sugar, wheat flour, and jam or currant jelly.
steps: Wash the butter and stir until white and fluffy, then add the sugar together with the eggs, one at a time, and stir the mixture for 10 minutes.
Lastly stir in the flour, which should be sifted and well mixed with the baking powder.
Line a small baking sheet with low edges with white, buttered paper (15 gr. butter).
Spread the batter onto it to a cake of approx. 1/2 cm. thickness and bake in a warm oven until it has a beautiful golden-brown color.
Turn the cake out immediately onto a paper sprinkled with granulated sugar, brush with warm jam or stirred currant jelly and roll up quickly.
Let the cake cool and then cut across into 1 1/2 cm. thick slices.
Alternatively, the cake can be cut in half, spread a cream made of well-washed butter, sugar and arrack or punch or vanilla cream or jelly on one half, and place the other half on top.

The cake is then cut out with small measures or cut into small square, diagonal or oblong pieces, which are glazed in different colors and garnished with finely chopped orange peel, sweet almond or pistachio, or with walnuts or hazelnuts.
These cakes are served with glace, together with small rings of butter dough or small canapés.

title: Ränklor som salad (Medlars as Salad)
description: A salad made with medlars, vinegar, and water.
steps: Rinse the fruit and prick with a silver fork (the skin will not burst in cooking). Cut off the stems somewhat.
Mix the water and salt cold together, place the fruit in the brine and let it sit for two days.
Remove it and let it sit in fresh water for one day.
Place the fruit on the heat in new, fresh water. As the berries float up, remove them with a slotted spoon and place them in vinegar-mixed water.
When they are completely cold, place them on linen to drain.
From the sugar and water, boil a clear, thick syrup. Let the syrup cool and then pour it over the berries.
Sprinkle the top layer with sugar (otherwise the berries will be dark).
The next day, pour off the syrup, boil it up, let it cool and pour it over the fruit.
Repeat the following day. Now let the syrup stand over the berries for 3-4 days.
Pour off the syrup once more, let it come to a boil, then carefully place the berries back in.
Bring the jam to a light boil, remove the berries with a slotted spoon and place them in jars.
Let the syrup boil down further until it is thick.
Cool it and pour it over the fruit.
Tie the jars and store in a cool place.

title: Rådjurssadel (Roasted Venison Saddle)
description: Prepared with lard, white pepper, and broth.
steps: With a sharp knife, remove all membranes on the back without any meat being included.
Lard the saddle with finely shredded lard strips, dipped in a mixture of salt and pepper.
Place in a long pan, cover with butter distributed in flakes, set in a warm oven and let stand 15 minutes.
Then add the boiling broth and cream and let roast until tender, or about 1 1/2 hours, basting every 10 minutes, otherwise it will dry out.
Cut the saddle as mutton saddle, garnish with browned potatoes, small tarts filled with lingonberry jelly, or with vegetable salad in small shells of raw cabbage leaves.
Serve with reduced sauce (see no. 429), added with 1 tbsp. lingonberry jelly.
From the saddle, cutlets can be cut out, which are fried as veal cutlets, with or without breading.
Serve with stewed mushrooms or champignons, potato croquettes or chestnut purée.

title: Rådjursstek (Roasted Roe Deer)
description: Prepared with lard, white pepper, and broth.
steps: Thaw the saddle as the roast in the previous recipe. Dry it well and remove all membranes carefully, then lard it thickly with finely cut lard strips dipped in salt.

Brown the butter in a roasting pan, place the saddle in it with the meat side down and brown beautifully, then turn it and dilute first with the boiling broth, then with the boiling cream or milk, and let it roast with a tightly closed lid until tender, about 2 1/2 hours, basting every 10 minutes or so.

Place the saddle on a warm platter, loosen the meat neatly on both sides of the backbone, place on a cutting board and cut across in beautiful slices, which are then laid back together on the saddle so that it looks whole.
Garnish with browned potatoes, salad or parsley and serve with lingonberry jelly and reduced sauce.

title: Rådjursstek (Roebuck Roast)
description: Prepared with lard, white pepper, and broth.
steps: The roebuck should be young, not weighing more than 15-20 kg before it is skinned, in order to be juicy and tender.
The meat should hang for 4-5 days before it is prepared.

When the roebuck is to be skinned, the skin is loosened around the knee joint, it is hung by the hind legs and the skin is ripped open with a sharp knife from the inside of the leg through the belly and up to the head.
The skin is pulled off, the head is cut off and the entrails are removed.
It is then cut up like mutton, but with a saddle instead of two rows of chops.

The roast is beaten with a damp club, the membranes are pulled off, it is larded, rubbed with the rest of the spices and roasted in a pot and extended with the boiling broth and cream and is ready after 2-2 1/2 hours.

The roast is cut, laid on a warm plate, poured over with a couple of tablespoons of sauce, garnished with browned potatoes, salad and parsley and served with redcurrant jelly, apple sauce and reduced sauce, supplemented with 1 tablespoon redcurrant jelly.

title: Rågsiktbröd (Rye Sifted Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with rye, wheat flour, and yeast.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in a little of the lukewarm milk.
Place the sifted rye flour in a bowl, add the lukewarm milk with vigorous stirring, and stir in the dissolved yeast, then beat the dough smooth and glossy.
Place in a warm spot to rise to double size.
Add the well-washed and stirred butter, syrup, the crushed spices and the finely chopped orange peel, and work in the wheat flour until the dough becomes quite firm.
Let it rise again.
Finally work the dough on the baking board and shape into oblong buns, place on heated and floured cloths to rise.
When well risen, place on buttered sheets, brush with cold water and bake in a warm oven.
During baking, brush the buns twice with hot water, likewise when the finished buns are removed from the oven.
Cover them well so that the crust does not become too hard.

Dip the mold briefly in lukewarm water.
Turn out the pudding and serve with vanilla sauce or cream.
Preferably make this the day before.

title: Rödkål (Red Cabbage)
description: Prepared with cabbage, juice or lemon or beet or vinegar, and butter.

ingredients.name: juice of 1 lemon or 3 tablespoons beet vinegar or regular vinegar
ingredients.sourceText: juice of 1 lemon or 3 tablespoons beet vinegar or regular vinegar

steps: Remove the outer leaves of the cabbage head, loosen the remaining leaves from the core, cut away the thickest part of the main vein, and cut the cabbage into fine strips.
Melt the butter in a pot, add the cabbage, and add the seasonings together with the lemon juice. Let the cabbage cook slowly with a closed lid for about 2 hours, stirring it often.
Let the cabbage cook for 15 minutes without a lid and with constant stirring.

Taste and season with more butter, spices and lemon juice if needed. Serve with fatty meat dishes such as Prague ham, goose and duck. If desired, the cabbage can be cooked with 1/2 teaspoon caraway and seasoned with a little red wine or red currant juice.

title: Rökt, Kokt Skinka i Gelé (Smoked, Boiled Ham in Aspic)
description: Prepared with aspic, smoked ham, and gelatin.
steps: Soak the ham in plenty of cold water overnight to remove salt.
Place the ham skin-side up in cold water and simmer slowly until tender, approximately 3 1/2 hours. It is done when the small bone on the ham hock loosens easily.
Let the ham cool in its cooking liquid, then transfer it to an elongated platter and remove the skin.
Prepare the white and red aspic as in recipe no. 181. If the red aspic is too light, color it with a little carmine.
Slice the ham into even, attractive slices and lay them back on the bone so the ham appears whole.
Gradually pour the white aspic over the slices so they hold together and the ham becomes beautifully glazed.
When the white aspic has set completely, garnish the ham with the red aspic, piped through a fluted paper cone to form flowers and swags.
Cut the beans into stems and leaves.
Garnish the bone of the ham with crinkled paper and the platter with chopped aspic, aspic croutons, and greens.
Serve as a course dish with vegetable salad or stuffed tomatoes.
